original_text:
80% of Data Engineering Candidates Struggle with These 14 Interview Topics. Learn them and stand out.

1. Batch vs Streaming
Tradeoff: Batch is cost-efficient; Streaming is real-time. Pick wrong and SLAs/costs go off-track.
Interview Q: How would late-arriving events affect your daily reports?
Drill: Build a Spark batch job to S3. Rebuild it with Kafka + Flink. Compare freshness vs compute cost.

2. Columnar Formats (Parquet, ORC)
Why: Column pruning & compression = 90% less I/O.
Pitfall: Tiny files destroy performance.
Drill: Compare SQL scan over CSV vs Parquet with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.

3. Partitioning & Clustering
Why: Partitioning skips data; clustering reduces scan depth.
Pitfall: Too many partitions = thousands of tiny tasks.
Drill: Load logs partitioned by dt, then cluster by user_id. Observe task parallelism.

4. Schema Evolution
Why: Real-world data changes constantly.
Interview Q: “How do you evolve a schema without breaking consumers?”
Drill: Use Avro + Confluent Registry to evolve a schema. Test compatibility modes.

5. Change Data Capture (CDC)
Why: Keeps data fresh without full reloads.
Pitfall: Out-of-order events if binlog tracking fails.
Drill: Stream MySQL binlogs with Debezium → Kafka → PostgreSQL. Check consistency.

6. Watermarks & Late Data
Why: Event-time processing needs cutoffs.
Interview Q: How do you handle 2-hour-late events in a 1-hour window?
Drill: In Flink, simulate delayed events. Use allowedLateness. Track watermark state.

7. Idempotent Writes
Why: Retries shouldn’t duplicate records.
Drill: In Delta Lake, write with MERGE. Replay Kafka topic—verify counts remain stable.

8. Data Lineage & Metadata
Why: You can’t debug metrics if you don’t know what changed them.
Drill: Use OpenLineage or Marquez with Airflow. Track lineage for one KPI pipeline.

9. Orchestration (Airflow)
Why: Manual scripts fail silently. DAGs bring order.
Interview Q: How would you prevent accidental re-runs?
Drill: Convert scripts to Airflow DAGs. Use depends_on_past + max_active_runs.

10. Incremental vs Full Loads
Why: Full loads waste time and money; incrementals are harder but efficient.
Drill: Redesign an S3-to-Redshift pipeline to use manifest-based incremental load.

11. Data Skew
Why: One hot key can kill your job.
Interview Q: Why did one task take 10x longer?
Drill: Introduce skew in a Spark join. Observe stage duration. Fix with salting or repartitioning.

12. Backpressure in Streaming
Why: Streams crash if source outruns processing.
Drill: Overwhelm a Kafka → Spark Structured Streaming job. Tune maxOffsetsPerTrigger.

13. NoSQL (MongoDB, DynamoDB)
Why: Not all data fits in rows and columns.
Q: When would you use NoSQL over a relational DB?
Drill: Build a product catalog in MongoDB. Run flexible queries on nested fields.

14. Data Security & Access Control
Why: Data breaches = instant failure.
Q: How do you control access to S3 or ADLS?
Drill: Configure IAM (AWS) or RBAC (Azure) to grant object-level access.

#DElveWithVani

ai_analysis.summary: This technical Data Engineering interview-preparation post outlines 14 topics: batch versus streaming, Parquet and ORC, partitioning and clustering, schema evolution, Change Data Capture, watermarks and late data, idempotent writes, lineage and metadata, Airflow orchestration, incremental and full loads, data skew, streaming backpressure, NoSQL, and security. It provides a rationale, common pitfall, and suggested drill for each area. The post describes batch processing as cost-efficient, streaming processing as real-time, and column pruning and compression as producing 90% less I/O, although it does not provide evidence for the numerical I/O claim.

interview_questions.question: What tradeoff should you evaluate when choosing batch or streaming processing?
interview_questions.answer:
Batch processing is presented as cost-efficient, while streaming processing provides real-time freshness.
The choice should account for service-level agreements, freshness requirements, and compute cost.

interview_questions.question: How can Parquet or ORC improve a query workload, and what performance pitfall should be monitored?
interview_questions.answer:
Column pruning and compression are presented as ways to reduce I/O, with the post claiming 90% less I/O.
Tiny files can destroy performance, so their presence should be monitored.
A SQL scan over CSV and Parquet can be compared with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.

interview_questions.question: How should partitioning and clustering be used without creating excessive tiny tasks?
interview_questions.answer:
Partitioning can skip data, while clustering can reduce scan depth.
Logs can be partitioned by dt and clustered by user_id so task parallelism can be observed.
Too many partitions can create thousands of tiny tasks.

interview_questions.question: How would you evolve a schema without breaking existing consumers?
interview_questions.answer:
The post frames schema evolution as necessary because real-world data changes constantly.
It proposes Avro with Confluent Registry and testing compatibility modes.

interview_questions.question: Why use Change Data Capture, and how would you validate a Debezium pipeline from MySQL binlogs through Kafka to PostgreSQL?
interview_questions.answer:
CDC keeps destination data fresh without full reloads.
Out-of-order events are a stated pitfall when binlog tracking fails.
The proposed flow streams MySQL binlogs with Debezium through Kafka into PostgreSQL and checks consistency.

interview_questions.question: How should a Flink job handle events that arrive two hours late in a one-hour window?
interview_questions.answer:
Event-time processing needs cutoffs, and the scenario includes data beyond the expected one-hour window.
The suggested drill simulates delayed events, uses allowedLateness, and tracks watermark state.

interview_questions.question: How can Delta Lake be used to verify that replaying a Kafka topic produces idempotent writes?
interview_questions.answer:
The objective is to prevent retries from duplicating records.
Use MERGE in Delta Lake, replay the Kafka topic, and verify that record counts remain stable.

interview_questions.question: What should you track to diagnose a change in a KPI metric?
interview_questions.answer:
Track lineage and metadata because metrics cannot be debugged without knowing what changed them.
The post suggests using OpenLineage or Marquez with Airflow for one KPI pipeline.

interview_questions.question: How would you convert manual scripts into an Airflow workflow that is safer to rerun?
interview_questions.answer:
Manual scripts can fail silently, whereas DAGs provide order.
Convert the scripts into Airflow DAGs.
The drill calls for configuring depends_on_past and max_active_runs when addressing rerun behavior.

interview_questions.question: When is a manifest-based incremental load preferable to a full S3-to-Redshift load?
interview_questions.answer:
Full loads waste time and money, while incremental loads are harder but more efficient.
The suggested redesign uses a manifest-based incremental load for the S3-to-Redshift pipeline.

interview_questions.question: Why can one task in a Spark join run much longer than the others, and which fixes are suggested?
interview_questions.answer:
A hot key can introduce data skew and make one task disproportionately slow.
Introduce skew in a Spark join and observe the stage duration.
Address the skew with salting or repartitioning.

interview_questions.question: How can backpressure be controlled when a Kafka source overwhelms Spark Structured Streaming?
interview_questions.answer:
Backpressure occurs when the source outruns processing, and the post warns that streams can fail in this situation.
The suggested drill deliberately overwhelms the job and tunes maxOffsetsPerTrigger.

interview_questions.question: When would MongoDB or DynamoDB be considered instead of a relational database?
interview_questions.answer:
NoSQL may be considered when the data does not fit neatly into rows and columns.
A practical drill builds a product catalog in MongoDB and runs flexible queries against nested fields.

interview_questions.question: How can object-level access to data in S3 or ADLS be controlled?
interview_questions.answer:
Use IAM in AWS or RBAC in Azure to grant object-level access.
Access control is presented as essential because data breaches can cause immediate failure.
